title: Health Education Curriculum Update - Erin's Law
source_title: Marshall E-News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
IMPORTANT 

UPDATES 

& 

REMINDERS IMPORTANT UPDATES & REMINDERS

Health Education Curriculum Update - SB 288-Erin's Law The Ohio Department of Education and Workforce (DEW), formally called the Ohio Department of Education, has shared with public schools across the state Senate Bill 288. This legislation requires that health education curricula be updated to include (K-12/developmentally appropriate) prevention education information in the areas of sexual abuse and sexual violence for students in public schools.As promised, the district is providing an opportunity for families to review the curriculum, and parents may opt their students out of the lessons if they choose.  For more information from the Ohio Department of Education- Click HERE. Instruction occurs annually. This year the district will conduct these updates with students October 12-26, 2026.K-3 Curriculum- Click HERE4-6 Curriculum- Click HERE7-8 Curriculum- TMSSocial Inclusion: Click HEREDating Violence: Click HERESuicide Prevention: Click HERE9-12 Curriculum - THS will share their videos in three successive weeks. Social Inclusion: Click HEREDating Violence / Healthy Relationships: Click HERESuicide Prevention: Click HEREContact your student's building and school counselor with any questions.

summary: Ohio Senate Bill 288 (Erin's Law) requires updated health education curriculum including **developmentally appropriate prevention education on sexual abuse and sexual violence** for K-12 students. Instruction will occur **October 12-26, 2026** across all grade levels. Families can review curriculum materials online (links provided for K-3, 4-6, 7-8, and 9-12 covering topics like social inclusion, dating violence, and suicide prevention), and parents may opt their students out. Contact your student's school counselor with questions.

blocks.content:
A 

NOTE 

FROM 

OUR 

SCHOOL 

COUNSELOR A NOTE FROM OUR SCHOOL COUNSELOR

SHARE YOUR PASSION AT SPARK DAY!Marshall will be hosting our bi-annual SPARK Day on Friday November 6th. We are looking for presenters who are passionate about a hobby or career. We will have a morning session for 3rd-5th graders from 9:30 - 11:15 and an afternoon session for K - 2nd graders from 1:30 - 3:00. If you or someone you know is willing to participate, please contact Teresa Peter at petert@talawanda.org or 513-273-3628.WHAT WE ARE LEARNING IN SECOND STEP:We have begun Second Step lessons at all grade levels. Kindergarten through 3rd graders are focusing on how to be good learners with an emphasis on practicing, learning from mistakes, positive self-talk and asking for help. 4th graders are focused on goal setting and have a group project to work on. 5th graders are focusing on problem solving using the STEP process. Please ask your child about what they've learned from Second Step this month.

summary: The **Title I Reading Corner Classroom** provides daily 30-minute small-group reading instruction for K-3 students at Marshall Elementary. Teachers Lisa Dyer and Shawna Dalton work with students on letter naming, phonemic awareness, phonics, vocabulary, fluency, comprehension, and writing. Students are selected based on assessments given at the beginning of the school year and in December, and are released from the program when they consistently meet grade-level benchmarks. Parents are welcome to contact teachers with questions about their child's reading progress.

title: Volunteer and Visitor Policy Requirements
source_title: Marshall E-News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
VOLUNTEER 

& 

VISITOR 

POLICY VOLUNTEER & VISITOR POLICY

As we continue with our volunteer policy this year, please remember that any adult volunteer who wishes to enter the school building must have a volunteer application on file with the office every school year. After a parent’s second visit to the building, they are required to complete fingerprinting and a background check through the Central Registration Office. Please plan to complete this process at least 3 weeks prior to the event. This allows adequate time for the background check to be completed and for the appropriate information to be provided to the school administrator for planning purposes. Once completed, your background check is valid for 5 years.Central Registration Office:Ruth Michael📞 513-273-3101We appreciate your understanding and cooperation as we work to keep our students, staff, and school community safe. Public schools have implemented these regulations to comply with state and federal safety requirements regarding volunteers and visitors in schools.

summary: All adult volunteers must have a volunteer application on file with the office each school year. After a second visit, parents must complete **fingerprinting and a background check** through the Central Registration Office at least **3 weeks prior** to their event. Background checks are valid for **5 years**. Contact Ruth Michael at **513-273-3101** for Central Registration.

& 

INFORMATION  NEWS & INFORMATION

Hello, Families!We hope everyone has had a wonderful week! It has been great seeing our students settling into the school year and building new routines. A quick reminder that there will be no school on Monday or Tuesday. We hope your family enjoys the long weekend, and we look forward to welcoming everyone back on Wednesday refreshed and ready to learn.Thank you to everyone who has supported our PTG fundraiser so far. We truly appreciate your generosity and involvement. Your support helps make so many wonderful opportunities possible for our students and staff. Today was also a lot of fun as we had Pajama Day! It was wonderful seeing students and staff dressed in their cozy pajamas while enjoying a day of learning together. Thank you to everyone who participated and helped make it a fun day.Have a safe and relaxing long weekend. We look forward to seeing everyone back at school on Wednesday!Stephanie JonesPrincipal

summary:
Nurse Tonja welcomes students back and provides important health reminders for the school year:
- **Medications**: Required forms must be completed and medications brought by parent/guardian (not in backpacks)
- **Contact Information**: Update the school with current phone numbers and emergency contacts
- **Extra Clothes**: Keep spare clothes at school for accidents
- **Illness Policy**: Keep children home if they have fever, vomiting, diarrhea, or are too sick to learn
- **Immunizations**: Ensure all required immunizations are up-to-date
- **Medical Conditions**: Notify the nurse of any new diagnoses, allergies, or health concerns
